## About this course

A reproducible project can be re-run, understood and shared by other people. It is also easier for you to return to months later.

This course introduces the practical habits that make this possible. It covers project structure, documentation, Quarto reports, virtual environments and sharing data.

The course takes about two hours. It is taught mainly through live demos and hands-on exercises, and notes are provided for reference.

## Prerequisites

- Some experience of working with data
- If you code: you have an IDE of your choice and can run simple terminal / CLI commands

Please follow our [installation instructions](https://bristol-training.github.io/data-science-project-setup/) before the course.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this course, you will be able to:

1. Organise a project into raw data, processed data, code and outputs, and explain why raw data is never edited.
2. Write a README and a data dictionary that help others understand and use your project.
3. Explain why Quarto helps reproducibility, and build a report that updates when the data changes.
4. Explain why environments matter, and record the software a project needs so it can be re-run on another computer.
5. Check a dataset against the Q-FAIR principles, and know where to find out more about sharing data.

## Course outline

| Section | Topic | Time |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Project structures | 30 min |
| 2 | Documentation & Quarto | 45 min |
| 3 | Virtual environments | 30 min |
| 4 | Sharing data: Q-FAIR | 15 min |

Sections 1 to 3 each have slides, live demos and a hands-on exercise. Section 4 is a shorter overview, with a short exercise.
